subject: FinEx post-call: throughput & latency qualification
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sahil Rao <sahil@finexops.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinEx post-call: throughput & latency qualification

Thanks for the call today — great to meet the FinEx infra and ops team. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned on sizing for the pilot: 

Summary of call:
- Primary use case: real-time transaction enrichment for compliance screens (low-latency inference on incoming transaction text)
- Model type: open LLM (2.7B) for classification + 13B for fallback summarization/QA
- Target latency SLO: 200ms p50, 400ms p95 for the classification path (no streaming). Summarization path can be async (up to 2s).
- Expected workload (ballpark): steady-state 150 QPS, bursts up to 1,200 QPS for short windows (10-20s).
- Average input: ~80 tokens per request; summarization path averages 600 tokens output.
- Concurrency: expected 20 concurrent long-running summarization jobs; classification path concurrency driven by QPS above.

Neha (action items):
- Rafael to send throughput-sizing worksheet (tokens/sec and GPU estimates).
- FinEx to confirm exact QPS distribution (per region) and percent of requests that will trigger summarization path.
- Marissa to include recommended instance/quantization combinations for pilot.

Could you reply with the finer-grain numbers below so we can finalize sizing? Specifically:
1) Typical requests per minute/hour and expected distribution over the day
2) Percent of classification responses that escalate to summarization or streaming
3) Any hard SLOs for p99 or error budgets we should be aware of

Thanks — aiming to get a draft pilot capacity plan over the next 48 hours.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-pricing-proposal.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sahil Rao <sahil@finexops.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Anika Bose <anika@finexops.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinEx post-call: throughput & latency qualification

Thanks Neha — appreciate the recap. Adding the numbers you asked for below (these are our best estimates from the traffic team):

Workload breakdown:
- Steady state: 9,000 requests/minute (~150 QPS) for classification.
- Peak burst: up to 72,000 requests/minute (~1,200 QPS) for 10-20s on settlement windows. These are short bursts that happen ~4x/day.
- 8% of classification requests (~12 QPS steady, ~96 QPS burst) escalate to the summarization path.

Request/response sizes:
- Classification: avg 80 tokens in, ~20 tokens out.
- Summarization/fallback: avg 100 tokens in, ~600 tokens out.

Latency SLOs:
- Classification (hard): p50 <= 200ms, p95 <= 400ms, p99 <= 700ms. Very sensitive — sub-1s p99 is a blocker.
- Summarization: p95 <= 2s is acceptable.

Concurrency:
- At peak bursts, we estimate ~200 concurrent in-flight classification requests and up to 40 concurrent summarization jobs.

Streaming:
- We do not require streaming for classification. For summarization, we can accept non-streaming responses, but would like to evaluate streaming in a later phase to improve perceived latency.

Let me know if you need per-region splits — for pilot we'll route traffic from US-east only.

Thanks,
Sahil Rao
FinEx — Platform Ops
[signature: FinEx | ops@finexops.com]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sahil Rao <sahil@finexops.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinEx post-call: throughput & latency qualification

Perfect — this is exactly what we needed, thanks. A few clarifying questions before Rafael shares the workbook: 

1) During the 1,200 QPS bursts, are the 8% escalations evenly distributed across the burst window or concentrated at the end of the window? If concentrated, that has implications for peak concurrency.
2) For summarization outputs (~600 tokens), are those returned synchronously in-path or queued for async workers? You mentioned earlier the downstream pipeline can handle async; confirming for sizing.
3) Any headroom requirement (e.g., want 2x capacity reserved for safety) for the pilot?

Next steps: Rafael will drop the throughput workbook + recommended GPU counts (with options for quantization/float16) to this thread. We'll aim to propose a pilot configuration that meets p95/p99 SLOs for classification while keeping costs reasonable.

Best,
Neha

To: Sahil Rao <sahil@finexops.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinEx post-call: throughput & latency qualification

Thanks Sahil — good detail. Attached is the throughput-sizing workbook with three pilot options:
- Option A (cost-optimized): 2x gpus (quantized 8-bit) sized for steady-state with autoscale for bursts (may push p95 to ~450ms in worst-case bursts).
- Option B (balanced): 4x gpus (mixed-precision fp16 for classification, q8 for summarization) aiming to meet p95 400ms during typical bursts.
- Option C (SLA-focused): 8x gpus (fp16 + extra headroom) to keep p95 & p99 well within targets even during back-to-back bursts.

Key assumptions in workbook:
- Classification tokens/sec calculated from 150 QPS * 100 tokens/request (in+out) = 15k tokens/sec steady; burst tokens/sec ~120k tokens/sec.
- Summarization steady tokens/sec ~12k (12 QPS * 1000 tokens/request), burst ~96k.
- We included a conservative 1.5x overhead for network/serialization delays and peak jitter.

Questions for FinEx to finalize sizing:
1) Confirm whether summarization will be sync (in-path) or queued async. If async, we can reduce headroom for classification paths.
2) Confirm any regulatory constraints on model hosting/location and whether private deployment (VPC) is required for pilot.

I'll follow up with a short doc that maps each option to expected latency percentiles and cost per hour. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min session early next week to walk the workbook line-by-line.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
